meta.blurb: A king in a mask, a club for red-haired men, a goose with a jewel inside, a bedroom where a girl hears a whistle at night. Twelve cases come to 221B Baker Street, and Holmes sees what everyone else misses.
meta.bible: Sherlock Holmes: the consulting detective of Baker Street; calm, clever, vain, kind when it matters. Dr John Watson: his friend and the narrator, a doctor. The twelve cases in order: A Scandal in Bohemia; The Red-Headed League; A Case of Identity; The Boscombe Valley Mystery; The Five Orange Pips; The Man with the Twisted Lip; The Blue Carbuncle; The Speckled Band; The Engineer's Thumb; The Noble Bachelor; The Beryl Coronet; The Copper Beeches. Bohemia: the King of Bohemia, who comes in a mask; Irene Adler, the clever singer who beats Holmes; Godfrey Norton, her husband. The Red-Headed League: Jabez Wilson, pawnbroker with red hair; Vincent Spaulding, his assistant, really John Clay; Duncan Ross; Saxe-Coburg Square; the City and Suburban Bank; Inspector Jones; Mr Merryweather. Case of Identity: Mary Sutherland; Hosmer Angel; Mr Windibank, her stepfather. Boscombe Valley: Charles McCarthy, killed; James McCarthy, his son; John Turner; Alice Turner; Ballarat; Inspector Lestrade; Herefordshire. Five Orange Pips: John Openshaw; Elias Openshaw; the ship Lone Star. Twisted Lip: Neville St Clair; Hugh Boone, a beggar; Isa Whitney; Upper Swandam Lane. Blue Carbuncle: Peterson, the doorman; Henry Baker; the Countess of Morcar; John Horner; James Ryder; Mr Breckinridge; Covent Garden. Speckled Band: Helen Stoner; Julia Stoner, her dead sister; Dr Grimesby Roylott, her stepfather; Stoke Moran. Engineer's Thumb: Victor Hatherley; Colonel Lysander Stark; Eyford. Noble Bachelor: Lord Robert St Simon; Hatty Doran; Frank Moulton; Flora Millar; Hyde Park. Beryl Coronet: Alexander Holder, a banker; his son Arthur; his niece Mary; Sir George Burnwell; Streatham. Copper Beeches: Violet Hunter; Jephro Rucastle; Mrs Rucastle; Mr and Mrs Toller; Carlo; Alice Rucastle; Mr Fowler. Baker Street, London, Scotland Yard, the Thames, England. Voice and tone: lively, clear and clever, each case a small, complete puzzle; deaths are stated plainly, with no gore; Holmes is sometimes merciful. Beat 50 closes the whole book. Added for the full-length book: Count Von Kramm (the King's false name); Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, Grand Duke of Cassel-Felstein; Scandinavia; Irene Adler, born in New Jersey, sang in Warsaw and at La Scala; Godfrey Norton of the Inner Temple; Briony Lodge, St John's Wood; the Church of St Monica, Edgware Road; Hercules; Nonconformist; Bohemia. Also added: Inspector Bradstreet of Scotland Yard; Hayling, a missing engineer; Reading; Paddington; Berkshire; Aloysius Doran, a rich American of California; the Duke of Balmoral; St George's Church, Hanover Square; Lancaster Gate; the Serpentine; Apaches; Frank Moulton, Hatty's first husband; Threadneedle Street; Streatham; the Beryl Coronet, thirty-nine beryls; Mary, Holder's niece; Westaway's agency; Winchester; Copper Beeches; Edward, the Rucastles' small son; Carlo, the mastiff; Mr Fowler, who marries Alice; Southampton; Mauritius; Walsall.

beats.scene: Watson climbs the stairs toward a lit window with a tall shadow
beats.summary: Married Watson sees Holmes's shadow on a lit blind, goes up, and is told he has grown heavier and gone back to work.

beats.scene: Holmes points to a scratched shoe held out to the fire
beats.summary: Holmes explains his guesses from a scratched shoe, the smell of medicine and a bulge in a hat.

beats.scene: Holmes holds up a thick sheet of paper beside the stairs
beats.summary: Holmes says Watson sees but does not observe the seventeen steps, then hands him a note announcing a masked visitor.

beats.scene: Holmes holds the paper to the lamp as a carriage stops outside
beats.summary: The paper was made in Bohemia and the writer is a German, and then a carriage and pair arrives below.

beats.scene: A tall man in furs and a black mask fills the doorway
beats.summary: A huge man in rich clothes and a black mask enters and gives a false name, Count Von Kramm.

beats.scene: The masked man tears the black mask from his face
beats.summary: After a promise of two years' silence, Holmes names his visitor as the King of Bohemia, and the man tears off his mask.

beats.scene: The King sits with his head bowed in Holmes's armchair
beats.summary: The King tells of an old friendship with Irene Adler and of the photograph she holds as his wedding nears.

beats.scene: Holmes turns the pages of a large index book
beats.summary: Holmes finds Irene Adler in his index and hears that every attempt to get the photograph back has failed.

beats.scene: Gold coins and bank notes lie in a heap on a table
beats.summary: Holmes takes the case, the King pays three hundred pounds in gold and seven hundred in notes, and Holmes notes the address.

beats.scene: A drunken-looking groom talks to men in a stable lane
beats.summary: Disguised as a groom, Holmes hears in the stable lane that Irene has one visitor, a handsome lawyer named Godfrey Norton.

beats.scene: Two cabs race through the streets toward a church
beats.summary: Irene drives off after Norton, and Holmes follows both to the Church of St Monica in the Edgware Road.

beats.scene: A groom is pulled to the altar to sign a book
beats.summary: Holmes is dragged to the altar as a witness at Irene's wedding, and the bride gives him a golden sovereign.

beats.scene: Holmes lays out a plan on the table by the lamp
beats.summary: Holmes asks Watson to help with a plan, and Watson promises to do whatever is needed.

beats.scene: A clergyman in a black hat lies bleeding before the villa
beats.summary: Disguised as a gentle clergyman, Holmes is knocked down in a street fight outside the villa and carried inside.

beats.scene: Smoke pours from a window as a woman rushes to the wall
beats.summary: Watson throws the smoke rocket and cries fire, and Irene runs to the place where her photograph is hidden.

beats.scene: Two men walk home through dark streets under the lamps
beats.summary: Holmes sees where the photograph is, leaves quietly, and as the two walk home a young man bids him good night.

beats.scene: A maid in a doorway speaks to three men in the morning
beats.summary: At eight next morning, Holmes, Watson and the King find Briony Lodge empty, for Irene has gone to the Continent.

beats.scene: Holmes tears back a sliding panel in the wall
beats.summary: Holmes opens the hiding place and finds only a photograph of Irene in evening dress and a letter for himself.

beats.scene: Irene Adler's letter lies open on the table
beats.summary: In her letter Irene says she saw through the disguise, dressed as a man to follow Holmes, and has escaped with her husband.

beats.scene: The King smiles and holds out a ring to Holmes
beats.summary: The King is delighted, and Holmes asks only for Irene's photograph as his reward, for she will always be the woman to him.

beats.scene: A stout man with bright red hair sits opposite Holmes
beats.summary: One autumn day Watson finds Holmes with a stout visitor with fiery red hair, Jabez Wilson, whom Holmes reads at a glance.

beats.scene: Holmes points at a breast pin, a worn cuff and a fish tattoo
beats.summary: Holmes explains: the right hand is larger, the pin shows a Freemason, the cuff shows writing, and the tattoo and coin show China.

beats.scene: A dusty pawnshop with an assistant who climbs down to the cellar
beats.summary: Wilson keeps a small pawnbroker's shop in Saxe-Coburg Square; his assistant Vincent Spaulding works for half wages and loves photography.

beats.scene: Spaulding points at an advertisement in the newspaper
beats.summary: Spaulding shows Wilson the advertisement of the Red-Headed League, which offers four pounds a week to red-haired men.

beats.scene: A crowd of red-haired men fills a narrow street
beats.summary: Wilson and Spaulding find Fleet Street crowded with red-haired men of every shade, and Spaulding pushes through.

beats.scene: A small man with very red hair pulls Wilson's hair
beats.summary: Duncan Ross, a small man with redder hair, tests Wilson's hair by pulling it, and then chooses him over all the others.

beats.scene: A man copies pages at a bare table in an empty office
beats.summary: The work is to copy the Encyclopaedia from ten to two each day without leaving the office once, and Wilson accepts.

beats.scene: A heap of copied pages is stacked high on a bare table
beats.summary: For eight weeks he copies from A, Abbots to Attica, and each Saturday is paid four gold sovereigns.

beats.scene: A man stares at a card pinned to a locked office door
beats.summary: One morning the office is locked with a card saying that the League is dissolved, and nobody has heard of Duncan Ross.

beats.scene: Holmes sits cross-legged with a pipe, deep in thought
beats.summary: Holmes questions Wilson about his assistant, learns Spaulding has pierced ears and a white scar, and sits for three pipes to think.

beats.scene: Holmes taps the pavement with his stick before a small shop
beats.summary: Holmes and Watson walk to Saxe-Coburg Square, where Holmes thumps the pavement and then knocks at Wilson's shop.

beats.scene: A neat young man answers a shop door with a smile
beats.summary: Spaulding answers the door, and Holmes asks the way to the Strand but only looks at the knees of the man's trousers.

beats.scene: A tunnel runs below a street toward the walls of a bank
beats.summary: Holmes explains that the League was only a trick to keep Wilson away while the men dig a tunnel to the bank's vault.

beats.scene: Three men sit in a cab as it rolls through a dark street
beats.summary: Holmes sends for Scotland Yard's Peter Jones and the bank director Mr Merryweather, and they ride together to the bank that evening.

beats.scene: Stacks of wooden crates in a dark stone vault
beats.summary: In the bank's vault, Merryweather shows boxes of French gold, thirty thousand napoleons borrowed from the Bank of France, and they sit in darkness.

beats.scene: A thin line of light slips through the paving stones of a cellar
beats.summary: After an hour of waiting in darkness, a gleam of light appears between the stones, and a white hand comes through.

beats.scene: A man with a pistol climbs out of a hole and is seized
beats.summary: The thief climbs out, Holmes strikes his wrist with a hunting crop as he raises a pistol, and the police catch him.

beats.scene: A handsome thief is led away in handcuffs between two men
beats.summary: The thief is John Clay, a famous criminal who politely demands that the police say please, and he is led away.

beats.scene: Holmes and Watson sit before a fire with glasses and pipes
beats.summary: Back at Baker Street, Holmes explains the clues: the half wages, the cellar, the League, the knees and the Saturday plan.

beats.scene: Holmes sits at a window as London lights come on
beats.summary: Holmes says his life is a long effort to escape the dull routine of ordinary life, and that such cases are his reward.

beats.scene: A woman hesitates on the pavement below Holmes's window
beats.summary: Holmes tells Watson that life is stranger than fiction, and a hesitating woman on the pavement turns out to be a visitor.

beats.scene: Mary Sutherland sits in the client's chair, twisting her gloves
beats.summary: Miss Mary Sutherland enters, and Holmes guesses that she types for a living and is short-sighted.

beats.scene: A plain house with a middle-aged woman and a young-looking husband
beats.summary: Mary lives with her mother and her stepfather, Mr Windibank, who is only five years older than she is.

beats.scene: Dancers in a hall full of lanterns and a shy man in tinted glasses
beats.summary: At a gasfitters' ball, Mary meets Hosmer Angel, a quiet man in tinted glasses who calls while her stepfather is in France.

beats.scene: A couple walk through a park while a letter lies on a table
beats.summary: Hosmer walks with Mary and writes typed letters to the post office, and he asks her to marry him in secret before her stepfather returns.

beats.scene: A cab door stands open and the seat inside is empty
beats.summary: On the wedding morning, Hosmer rides in the cab with Mary to the church, but when it stops, he has vanished.

beats.scene: Holmes reads a typed letter by the window
beats.summary: Holmes studies the typed letters and asks for a description, Mary says that she will remain true, and Holmes tells her to forget him.

beats.scene: Holmes lights a pipe and writes one short note
beats.summary: Holmes writes a polite note asking Windibank to call, and he compares the typed letters by the lamp.

beats.scene: A pale man stands before Holmes, who locks the door
beats.summary: Windibank arrives and Holmes shows that his typewriter wrote the letters, and the stepfather confesses that he played Hosmer Angel.

beats.scene: A door swings open and an angry man runs down the stairs
beats.summary: Windibank says that no law has been broken and flees, and Holmes decides not to tell Mary, who would never believe him.

beats.scene: Watson reads a telegram at the breakfast table
beats.summary: A telegram from Inspector Lestrade asks Holmes and Watson to come to the west of England, and Watson's wife urges him to go.

beats.scene: A train runs through green fields toward the border hills
beats.summary: They take the train from Paddington to Ross, where Lestrade meets them and drives them to the Hereford Arms.

beats.scene: A small farmhouse and a larger house on a green hillside
beats.summary: Lestrade explains that Charles McCarthy rented a farm from John Turner, and that the two men had both lived in Australia.

beats.scene: A quiet pool among tall trees, with a girl picking flowers
beats.summary: On the afternoon of the crime, young Patience Moran sees Charles McCarthy and his son quarrelling in the wood beside the pool.

beats.scene: A young man kneels beside his father under the trees
beats.summary: James says he found his father dying, and that the dying man gasped two strange words, a rat.

beats.scene: A fair young woman stands in the doorway of an inn
beats.summary: Alice Turner calls on Holmes and says she is sure that James is innocent, whatever the police may say.

beats.scene: Holmes sits with papers and a pencil at the inn table
beats.summary: Holmes studies the evidence at the inn and notes that the cry and the dying word may point to a man from Australia.

beats.scene: Holmes bends over the grass beside the pool with a glass
beats.summary: At the pool Holmes examines the ground like a hound, studying the footprints of the dead man, his son and a stranger.

beats.scene: A cigar end lies beside a grey stone near the pool
beats.summary: Holmes reads the clues: the blow from a left-handed man, a limp, the ash of an Indian cigar, and the mark of a heavy boot.

beats.scene: Holmes speaks to Lestrade beside the grey stone
beats.summary: Holmes tells Lestrade the portrait of the killer, and Lestrade says that he is a practical man and will stay with his own theory.

beats.scene: A tall white-haired man sits wrapped in a rug by a window
beats.summary: Holmes and Watson call on John Turner, an old, sick man with a limp, at his house near the pool.

beats.scene: Holmes speaks quietly to an old man who covers his face
beats.summary: Holmes tells Turner that he knows the truth, and Turner, who knows he is dying, admits that he is the man.

beats.scene: A gold wagon train on a dusty road under hot sun
beats.summary: Turner tells how, years ago in Australia, he was a bushranger known as Black Jack of Ballarat and held up a convoy of gold.

beats.scene: A heavy man leans over a worried man at a table
beats.summary: McCarthy followed Turner home, forced him to give him a farm and a house, and demanded that Alice should marry his son.

beats.scene: Two men face each other beside a still pool in the afternoon
beats.summary: Turner went to the pool to meet McCarthy, and in a rage he struck him, not meaning to kill him, and then he fled.

beats.scene: A grey cloak lies on the grass and a man's hand takes it
beats.summary: James came upon his father, found the cloak and left, and Turner crept back and took his cloak before the police arrived.

beats.scene: A weak old man signs a paper at a table by lamplight
beats.summary: Holmes agrees not to use the confession unless James is found guilty, since Turner has only a few months to live.

beats.scene: A courtroom full of people and a young man in the dock
beats.summary: At the trial at the Assizes, James is found not guilty, since the evidence against him is weak and Holmes has shown how it can be explained.

beats.scene: An old man in a bed and a doctor beside him
beats.summary: Turner dies about seven months later, and James and Alice never learn of the dark cloud over their fathers' past.

beats.scene: Holmes sits silent in a railway carriage as green fields pass
beats.summary: On the train home, Holmes thinks of Turner and says that there, but for the grace of God, goes Sherlock Holmes.

beats.scene: Rain beats on the window of a lamplit sitting room
beats.summary: In a September gale Watson sits with Holmes in Baker Street, and a drenched young man named John Openshaw arrives.

beats.scene: A locked attic door at the top of a country house
beats.summary: Openshaw tells of his uncle Elias, a rich planter from Florida who lived at Horsham in fear and kept one room locked.

beats.scene: A letter with foreign stamps and five orange seeds on a table
beats.summary: In March a letter arrives from India with five dried orange pips and the letters K.K.K., and Elias turns white.

beats.scene: A bonfire of papers burns in an attic grate
beats.summary: Elias burns the contents of his attic and makes his will; seven weeks later he is found dead in the garden pool.

beats.scene: A man lies at the foot of a chalk pit in winter
beats.summary: Nearly two years later Joseph Openshaw receives the same envelope with five pips from Dundee and is found dead at the foot of a chalk pit.

beats.scene: A young man holds a new envelope up to the lamplight
beats.summary: John inherits, and after nearly three years of peace he receives the third envelope with five pips and the order to put the papers on the sundial.

beats.scene: Holmes reads a charred scrap of paper from a diary
beats.summary: Holmes studies a scrap of burned diary and tells Openshaw that K.K.K. was a secret society of the American South whose members hunted his uncle.

beats.scene: A young man buttons his coat and walks into the stormy night
beats.summary: Holmes sees that the three letters came from three ports, advises Openshaw to put the box on the sundial, and Openshaw goes out into the storm.

beats.scene: Holmes bends over a list of ships by the fire at dawn
beats.summary: Holmes finds the ship Lone Star in the shipping lists, and in the morning news comes that Openshaw has drowned, and Holmes vows to catch the men.

beats.scene: A ship's stern post with two letters floats in grey waves
beats.summary: Holmes finds that the Lone Star has sailed for Savannah, sends the pips to its captain, but the ship is lost in the equinoctial gales.

beats.scene: A worried woman stands at a doorway late at night
beats.summary: Kate Whitney comes to Watson's house late at night and begs him to find her husband, who is lost in an opium den.

beats.scene: A cab rolls through a dark East End street of shabby houses
beats.summary: Watson takes a cab to Upper Swandam Lane and finds the den, called the Bar of Gold, at the bottom of a flight of steps.

beats.scene: A pale man lies in a bunk with his head on his hands
beats.summary: Watson finds Isa Whitney, pale and shaking, and sends him home in a cab with a message for his wife.

beats.scene: A bent old man tugs at Watson's sleeve in the smoky room
beats.summary: As Watson turns to leave, a hand pulls his sleeve, and an old smoker tells him in a whisper to walk past and look back.

beats.scene: A thin old man straightens and winks in the smoky light
beats.summary: The old man is Holmes in disguise, and he explains that he is working on a case and will drive Watson to Lee in his trap.

beats.scene: A small trap with two horses waits outside a white villa
beats.summary: Holmes drives Watson to the house called The Cedars at Lee, where Mrs St Clair waits in a bright dress.

beats.scene: A smiling woman holds two small children's hands in a garden
beats.summary: Mrs St Clair says that her husband, a quiet gentleman of the City, left on Monday for London and did not come home.

beats.scene: A woman stands on a London street and looks up at a high window
beats.summary: Mrs St Clair goes to Swandam Lane, hears a cry above and sees her husband at a window, waving his hands, before he is pulled back.

beats.scene: A frightened woman is blocked by two men on a dark staircase
beats.summary: She runs into the building, but a sailor and a man at the door keep her out, and she goes for the police.

beats.scene: A scarred beggar with bright red hair stands before the police
beats.summary: Upstairs the police find only a beggar, Hugh Boone, with a twisted lip, and in the room Neville's clothes and a box of toy blocks.

beats.scene: A coat with heavy pockets lies in the mud of a river
beats.summary: Inspector Bradstreet's findings: blood on the window sill, and a coat weighted with coins found in the river below, but no body.

beats.scene: Mrs St Clair holds a short pencil note beside a lamp
beats.summary: Mrs St Clair shows Holmes a short note, in her husband's hand, that arrived that morning and begs her to wait without fear.

beats.scene: Holmes sits cross-legged on cushions as dawn light enters
beats.summary: Holmes smokes through the night on a nest of cushions, and at dawn wakes Watson to say that he has the answer.

beats.scene: Holmes and Watson drive through the early morning streets
beats.summary: They drive through the empty streets to Bow Street, where Inspector Bradstreet lets them see the prisoner.

beats.scene: A man sleeps on a bare bed with his face to the wall
beats.summary: Hugh Boone sleeps in his cell, and Holmes asks for water and a sponge to wash his face.

beats.scene: A scarred, red-haired man's face is wiped clean with a sponge
beats.summary: Holmes wipes the beggar's face, and the red hair and twisted lip come away, and he is revealed as Neville St Clair.

beats.scene: A pale man sits up on a bed with his hands over his face
beats.summary: The beggar admits he is St Clair and begs that his wife and children should not be disgraced.

beats.scene: A young man in a London newspaper office writes at his desk
beats.summary: St Clair tells how he was a reporter, once dressed as a beggar for an article, and he found that begging paid more than his job.

beats.scene: A man in a dim room paints a scar on his own lip
beats.summary: Money troubles drove St Clair to beg again, and he hid his new life from his wife by renting a room in Swandam Lane.

beats.scene: A man throws a heavy coat from a window toward the river
beats.summary: On the day of discovery, St Clair saw his wife in the street, threw the coat with its coins into the river and wrote the note, and he promises never to appear as Boone again.

beats.scene: Holmes lies on a sofa beside a shabby hat on a chair
beats.summary: Two days after Christmas, Watson finds Holmes on the sofa in a purple dressing gown, studying a battered old hat.

beats.scene: A tall man swings his stick, and a shop window shatters
beats.summary: Peterson, a commissionaire, tells how a man was attacked by roughs on Christmas morning, broke a window and ran away, dropping his goose and his hat.

beats.scene: A small card hangs from the leg of a plump white goose
beats.summary: A card on the goose reads For Mrs Henry Baker, and the initials H.B. are in the hat, but there are hundreds of Bakers in London.

beats.scene: Holmes holds a hat up to the window and studies the lining
beats.summary: Holmes reads the hat: its owner is clever, once well off, now poor, careless of himself, and his wife no longer loves him.

beats.scene: A man bursts through a door holding something in his open hand
beats.summary: Peterson rushes in and cries that the goose had a stone in it, a bright blue jewel in the palm of his hand.

beats.scene: A sparkling blue jewel lies between a finger and thumb
beats.summary: Holmes names the stone as the Blue Carbuncle, which belongs to the Countess of Morcar and for which a reward of a thousand pounds is offered.

beats.scene: A countess's dressing room with an empty jewel case
beats.summary: The jewel was stolen from the Countess of Morcar's room at the Hotel Cosmopolitan on 22 December, and a plumber, John Horner, was arrested.

beats.scene: Holmes locks a small blue stone away in a box
beats.summary: Holmes locks the jewel in his strong box, reflecting that the plumber may be innocent and that the goose must hold the answer.

beats.scene: A hand writes a notice at a desk beside a lamp
beats.summary: Holmes writes a notice for the evening newspapers asking Mr Henry Baker to call for his hat, and Peterson is sent to buy another goose.

beats.scene: A round-shouldered man in a frayed coat reaches for his old hat
beats.summary: Henry Baker calls, gets his hat, and Holmes says the goose is eaten, offers another, and learns that the bird came from a goose club at the Alpha Inn.

beats.scene: Two men in thick coats walk through a cold, lamplit street
beats.summary: Holmes sees that Baker knows nothing, and he and Watson set out into the frosty night to trace the goose.

beats.scene: A small corner pub with warm light and a man behind the bar
beats.summary: At the Alpha Inn, Holmes orders beer and asks the landlord about the geese, and learns that they come from a dealer at Covent Garden.

beats.scene: Crates of geese and rows of plucked birds under flaring lamps
beats.summary: At Covent Garden, Holmes finds Breckinridge at his stall, closing for the night and not eager to answer questions.

beats.scene: A gloved hand slides a gold coin onto a market counter
beats.summary: Holmes bets a sovereign that the goose was country bred, and Breckinridge shows his book to prove that it came from Mrs Oakshott of Brixton Road.

beats.scene: A thin, trembling man pleads at a stall while Holmes steps forward
beats.summary: A small, ferret-faced man asks Breckinridge the same question about the geese, and Holmes follows him and learns that his name is James Ryder.

beats.scene: Two men and a trembling third sit in a cab at night
beats.summary: Holmes takes Ryder in a cab to Baker Street, sits him by the fire and shows him the Blue Carbuncle, which he knows he has been seeking.

beats.scene: A man with his head in his hands before a fire
beats.summary: Ryder breaks down, and Holmes tells him that he knows all: the maid Catherine Cusack, the plumber and the jewel case.

beats.scene: A woman feeds a goose in a back yard of a Brixton house
beats.summary: Ryder tells how he went to his sister's house in Brixton, fed the stone to a goose, and killed the wrong bird.

beats.scene: A pale man runs from a door into a foggy street
beats.summary: Holmes opens the door and tells Ryder to go, since the man is frightened enough and the plumber will be cleared.

beats.scene: Holmes laughs by the fire with a pipe and a shaft of light
beats.summary: Holmes tells Watson that he is not paid to help the police do their work, that the season is for kindness, and starts a new inquiry, about a woodcock.

beats.scene: A veiled young woman sits shivering by Holmes's fire
beats.summary: One April morning Holmes wakes Watson early, and a veiled lady, Helen Stoner, tells them that it is fear and not cold that makes her shiver.

beats.scene: A grey old manor house with a crumbling wing among trees
beats.summary: Helen explains that she lives at Stoke Moran with her stepfather, Dr Roylott, the last of an old family that has lost all its money.

beats.scene: A tall angry man in a doctor's coat with a dark skin
beats.summary: Dr Roylott became a doctor in India, fell into a rage and beat his servant to death, served a prison term, and returned to England bitter.

beats.scene: A railway carriage wrecked on a bank beside a track
beats.summary: Helen's mother died in a railway accident, and Roylott took her money, and the twins stayed in the house, with a pet cheetah and a baboon in the grounds.

beats.scene: A young woman in a night dress listens at a bedroom door
beats.summary: Two years earlier Julia, who was soon to be married, came to Helen's room at midnight and asked whether she had heard a strange low whistle.

beats.scene: A door opens and a pale girl falls against a doorframe
beats.summary: That night Helen heard a scream and a clang, and Julia staggered out, crying that it was the band, the speckled band, and died in her sister's arms.

beats.scene: A woman at a table with a letter and a ring
beats.summary: Helen is now engaged herself, and two days earlier the builders started to repair her room, so that she moved into Julia's, where she heard the same whistle.

beats.scene: Holmes holds a woman's wrist and looks at five dark marks
beats.summary: Holmes sees five small bruises on her wrist, which she says her stepfather made, and decides to come to Stoke Moran that day.

beats.scene: A huge man fills the doorway of a sitting room in a dark coat
beats.summary: Dr Roylott bursts in, a huge man with a hunting crop, and he threatens Holmes and tells him to keep out of his affairs.

beats.scene: A great hand bends a steel poker over a hearth
beats.summary: Roylott threatens Holmes, bends the poker in his bare hands and storms out, and Holmes bends it straight again.

beats.scene: A dummy bell rope hangs beside a small round vent above a bed
beats.summary: At Stoke Moran, Holmes finds a bell rope that rings nothing, a vent into the next room, and a bed fixed to the floor.

beats.scene: An iron safe, a saucer of milk and a looped whip in a room
beats.summary: In Dr Roylott's room, Holmes notices an iron safe, a saucer of milk, a whip with a loop in the end and a chair beside the vent.

beats.scene: Two men sit at a window of an inn watching a distant house
beats.summary: Holmes tells Helen to lock herself in another room, with a lamp as a signal, and the two friends wait at the Crown Inn.

beats.scene: Two men sit in a dark room with a cane across one man's knees
beats.summary: At eleven the lamp shines, and the friends cross the lawn, climb in at the window and wait in the darkness with a cane and a pistol.

beats.scene: A faint light glows at the vent as Holmes lashes the rope
beats.summary: A glimmer shines at the vent, and a smell of oil fills the room, and then Holmes lashes at the bell rope and a whistle is heard.

beats.scene: Two men run through a dark passage toward a lit door
beats.summary: A horrible cry comes from the next room, and the friends run in to find Dr Roylott dead in his chair.

beats.scene: A man sits rigid in a chair with a speckled band round his head
beats.summary: Roylott sits dead in his chair, with a strange yellow band speckled with brown around his head, and the band moves.

beats.scene: A man drops a snake into an iron safe and shuts the door
beats.summary: Holmes loops the whip round the snake, throws it into the safe and shuts the door, and says that the doctor died within ten seconds of the bite.

beats.scene: Holmes and Watson in a train at dawn with a pale girl
beats.summary: Holmes tells how he reasoned, from the vent, the rope, the saucer of milk and the whistle, that a snake had been used, and he is not sorry.

beats.scene: A pale young woman is helped into a carriage at a station
beats.summary: Helen is taken safely to her aunt, and Holmes says that violence recoils upon the violent and that he does not feel that the doctor's death will weigh on his conscience.

beats.scene: A pale young man holds a bloody handkerchief round his hand
beats.summary: A station guard brings a pale young man with a bandaged hand to Watson's surgery early one summer morning.

beats.scene: A young engineer sits at a desk in a bare office
beats.summary: Hatherley tells how he was a poor young engineer with few clients, until a stranger named Colonel Lysander Stark visited him.

beats.scene: A stranger counts gold coins onto an engineer's desk
beats.summary: Stark offers fifty guineas for one night's work on a machine, but he demands total secrecy and says that Hatherley must travel by train to Eyford at night.

beats.scene: A dim little country railway station with a lamp and a carriage
beats.summary: Hatherley takes the train to Eyford, where Stark meets him in a closed carriage whose windows are frosted, so he cannot see out.

beats.scene: A woman with a lamp stands in the doorway of a lonely house
beats.summary: The carriage stops at a lonely house, where a woman in the hall begs Hatherley, in broken English, to leave before it is too late.

beats.scene: A huge iron press crouches in a stone cellar under a bright lamp
beats.summary: Stark takes Hatherley to a room with a huge hydraulic press and says that it has a fault, and he must find the leak.

beats.scene: An engineer looks closely at a bright metal film inside a cylinder
beats.summary: Hatherley finds metal dust and a shiny coating in the press, which shows that it presses metal, not earth, and Stark's face turns dark with rage.

beats.scene: A slow metal ceiling comes down on a man in a small stone room
beats.summary: Stark locks him into the press chamber and starts the machine, and the heavy iron roof begins to come slowly down.

beats.scene: A woman opens a hidden panel in a wall by lamplight
beats.summary: The woman from the hall slides back a hidden panel in the wall just in time, and Hatherley crawls through into a passage.

beats.scene: A man hangs from a window sill as a cleaver flashes above him
beats.summary: Hatherley climbs out through a window and hangs from the sill, and Stark, with a cleaver, cuts off his thumb, and he falls.

beats.scene: A wounded man lies in wet grass beneath a garden hedge at dawn
beats.summary: Hatherley wakes in the garden at dawn with his hand bleeding and ties it up with his handkerchief.

beats.scene: A bleeding man walks along an empty country lane at sunrise
beats.summary: He staggers out of the garden and along a lane toward the railway.

beats.scene: A pale man sits in an early morning train with a bandaged hand
beats.summary: At Eyford he takes the first train, and a railway guard helps him from Paddington to Watson's door.

beats.scene: Holmes sits among newspaper cuttings with a pair of scissors
beats.summary: Holmes listens with great interest, then reads out an old notice about a missing engineer named Hayling.

beats.scene: Holmes draws a circle on a railway map spread across a table
beats.summary: Holmes uses the map and the time of the drive to guess that the house is close to Eyford.

beats.scene: Five men sit in a train carriage with a map open on their knees
beats.summary: Holmes, Watson, Hatherley, Inspector Bradstreet and a plain-clothes man take the train to Eyford.

beats.scene: Black smoke rises above trees beyond a small railway station
beats.summary: At Eyford they see a column of smoke above the trees and learn that a house is on fire.

beats.scene: Villagers pass buckets along a line toward a burning house
beats.summary: The house is burning beyond saving, and Hatherley knows it as the house of the press.

beats.scene: Holmes crouches by a trampled garden path with a magnifying glass
beats.summary: Holmes finds the prints of a heavy man and a small woman who left before the fire.

beats.scene: Hatherley sits in a dim train carriage as evening falls
beats.summary: On the way home, Hatherley says that he has lost his thumb and his pay, and Holmes says that he has gained a story.

beats.scene: Holmes reads a letter with a great coat of arms beside a rainy window
beats.summary: On a wet autumn afternoon Holmes reads a letter from Lord St Simon and a newspaper notice of his marriage.

beats.scene: A tall nobleman with a stern face sits stiffly in Holmes's armchair
beats.summary: Lord St Simon arrives and tells of the quiet wedding at St George's, Hanover Square.

beats.scene: A bride's white flowers fall to the floor of a church aisle
beats.summary: The bride drops her flowers at church, and later Flora Millar, an old friend of the lord, makes a scene.

beats.scene: An empty bedroom with a white veil lying on the bed
beats.summary: The bride goes upstairs, puts on a long coat and bonnet, walks out of the house and does not come back.

beats.scene: A nobleman stands stiffly by a rainy window with his hat in his hand
beats.summary: Holmes asks about Hatty's past, and the lord leaves, more hurt in his pride than in his heart.

beats.scene: A detective sets a dripping bundle of silk on a table
beats.summary: Inspector Lestrade brings a wet bundle from the Serpentine, with a wedding gown, satin shoes and a veil.

beats.scene: A wet note lies beside a white satin shoe on a table
beats.summary: Inside the dress is a note signed with the letters F, H and M, and Lestrade has arrested Flora Millar.

beats.scene: A table laid with a cold supper in a lamp-lit sitting room
beats.summary: Holmes orders a cold supper for more than two, and says the gown in the water proves nothing.

beats.scene: A tall dark woman and a sunburned man stand in a doorway
beats.summary: Hatty arrives with Frank Moulton, her first husband, who was thought dead, and she tells how she saw him in the church.

beats.scene: A nobleman bows coldly and leaves a lamp-lit supper table
beats.summary: Hatty explains that she meant no harm, Lord St Simon departs in cold anger, and Holmes says a kind word for the lovers.

beats.scene: A stout banker rushes through falling snow toward a doorway
beats.summary: One winter morning the banker Alexander Holder rushes into Baker Street, wild with worry.

beats.scene: A banker locks a gold crown of green stones in a bank safe
beats.summary: A client of the highest rank has left the Beryl Coronet as security for a loan of fifty thousand pounds.

beats.scene: Three people sit at a quiet suburban dinner table
beats.summary: At Streatham live Holder, his wild son Arthur, his niece Mary and, as a frequent guest, the charming Sir George Burnwell.

beats.scene: A man in a dressing gown creeps along a dark corridor with a candle
beats.summary: Holder is woken in the night by a noise, creeps downstairs, and finds Arthur holding the broken coronet.

beats.scene: A young man stands silent while his father points at a broken crown
beats.summary: Arthur says nothing in his defence, and Holder calls the police.

beats.scene: Holmes and Holder walk through snow toward a villa gate
beats.summary: Holmes agrees to take the case and goes with Holder to Streatham.

beats.scene: A man studies footprints in fresh snow outside a villa
beats.summary: Holmes studies the snow outside the house and finds prints that show that someone had waited at the gate.

beats.scene: A gentle young woman pleads with a detective in a hall
beats.summary: Holmes speaks with Mary, who begs him to free Arthur, and she seems strangely sure that he is innocent.

beats.scene: A shabby loafer in a ragged coat slips out of a back gate
beats.summary: Holmes goes out in the disguise of a common loafer, and comes back that evening with the three missing stones.

beats.scene: A man at a desk reads a letter in a lonely study
beats.summary: Holmes tells the truth: Mary gave the coronet to Burnwell, Arthur followed and fought for it, and Mary has fled.

beats.scene: A young woman with a worried face sits in Holmes's armchair
beats.summary: Violet Hunter, a governess, comes to Holmes for advice about a post that pays too well.

beats.scene: A jolly stout man in a good coat sits in an employment office
beats.summary: At the agency, Mr Jephro Rucastle, a stout cheerful man, offers her a hundred and twenty pounds a year to teach one child.

beats.scene: A governess hesitates over a letter with a pair of scissors beside it
beats.summary: The catch is that she must cut her hair short, wear a dress he chooses and sit where he tells her.

beats.scene: A big old house stands behind copper-coloured trees in the evening
beats.summary: Violet goes to Copper Beeches, where the Rucastles welcome her, and the hair is cut and the blue dress put on.

beats.scene: A governess in a blue dress sits at a window with a laughing man
beats.summary: Rucastle sits her in a chair by the window, tells comic stories, and makes her laugh until her sides ache.

beats.scene: A pale silent woman sits in a dim hall beside a great mastiff
beats.summary: Mrs Rucastle is silent and sad, little Edward is cruel, and the dog Carlo is kept hungry and let loose at night.

beats.scene: A governess holds a small hand mirror toward a window
beats.summary: She sees through a hand mirror that a man is watching the house from the road, and Rucastle's laughter does not stop.

beats.scene: A woman draws a long chestnut curl from a drawer
beats.summary: In her room Violet finds a long coil of hair, exactly the colour and length of her own that was cut off.

beats.scene: A heavy locked door at the end of a dusty empty corridor
beats.summary: The rest of the house is empty, one wing is kept shut, and Mr Toller guards a locked room there.

beats.scene: A governess reads a message at a window with a dark garden below
beats.summary: Violet decides to find out the truth and sends Holmes a telegram.

beats.scene: Three people lean over a small table in a country inn
beats.summary: Holmes and Watson meet Violet at the inn, and Holmes guesses that she has been used as a stand-in for someone else.

beats.scene: A drunken man sleeps at a kitchen table beside an empty bottle
beats.summary: While Mr Rucastle is away, the Tollers are drunk, and Violet takes the keys.

beats.scene: A ladder rests below an open skylight in a bare empty room
beats.summary: They open the locked door and find an empty room with a skylight open and a ladder set against it.

beats.scene: A furious stout man bursts into a hall with a lamp
beats.summary: Mr Rucastle comes home early and finds them in the east wing, and he flies into a terrible rage.

beats.scene: A great dog bounds across a dark hallway toward a man
beats.summary: Rucastle roars for the dog, which is starving and wild, and the dog flies at his master's throat.

beats.scene: A thin servant aims a pistol at a snarling dog in a corridor
beats.summary: Toller, sobered, shoots the dog, and Rucastle lies badly hurt.

beats.scene: A rough man twists his cap before Holmes in a lamp-lit kitchen
beats.summary: Toller confesses that Alice, Rucastle's daughter, was shut up for refusing to sign away her money to him.

beats.scene: A young couple hurry toward a ship on a busy quay
beats.summary: Alice, helped by Mr Fowler, escapes, and they marry by special licence and sail for Mauritius.

beats.scene: Holmes and Watson look out of a railway carriage at green fields
beats.summary: On the train home, Holmes says that the lonely country can hide worse sins than the poor streets of London.

beats.scene: Watson sits at a desk with a pile of case notes by a lamp
beats.summary: Watson looks over his notes of the twelve cases and thinks of the friend who solved them.
